A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOLLEO study. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular optimization and docking experiments, multi-objective evaluations, and extensive appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds task evaluations, baseline comparisons, framework integrations, runtime measurements, and molecular-edit analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the original GPT-4, BioT5, and MoleculeSTM variants remain unchanged. Appendices D.2–D.3 add procedural adaptations: editing Augmented Memory's replay buffer, replacing Genetic GFN's genetic algorithm with MOLLEO, and replacing JANUS genetic operators.

E1.justification: Table 1 expands PMO coverage from 12 to 23 tasks, adding drug targets such as albuterol and celecoxib, additional MPO tasks, median1/median2 similarity objectives, another molecular formula, and valsartan_smarts. The three docking targets and existing multi-objective tasks are retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds Augmented Memory to Table 1 and evaluates DST on a task subset in Table A8. Augmented Memory and REINVENT also join the convergence comparison formerly shown in v1 Figure 5. Tables A9–A11 introduce comparisons against unmodified Augmented Memory, Genetic GFN, and JANUS.

E3.justification: The main oracle budgets, population settings, development tasks, and evaluation metrics are retained. Supplementary protocols add a single-round random-edit control, original-versus-random molecule similarity comparisons, framework substitution controls, and timing measurements. Appendix B newly documents objective normalization without establishing a change to the existing experiments.

E4.justification: Table A2 adds simultaneous LLM crossover and mutation ablations. Appendices D.2–D.6 newly examine transfer to other optimization frameworks, computational overhead, structural preservation during editing, and task-keyword exposure in training captions. These substantially extend the questions investigated; the earlier diversity analyses and molecule case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and use ± summaries and plotted uncertainty bands. v3 extends these reporting practices to additional results without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or increased run count.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive task, comparator, integration, and diagnostic results. For example, Table 1 newly reports GPT-4 MOLLEO scoring 0.867 ± 0.092 on valsartan_smarts while the other listed methods score zero. Among retained entries, GPT-4's QED result changes from 0.948 ± 0.004 to 0.948 ± 0.000. Tables 2 and 3 retain their numerical results; totals across the expanded task set are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation, Pareto-order and hypervolume definitions, and MoleculeSTM update and loss equations remain unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs; the added normalization explanation is implementation documentation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: chemistry-aware LLM genetic operators improve molecular optimization quality and oracle efficiency. The novelty and broad superiority claims are preserved; additional evaluations support or qualify these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4 newly explains how LLM overhead can increase runtime for cheap oracles and how API rate limits affect GPT-4. Appendices D.5–D.6 interpret molecular similarities as structural preservation and caption coverage as evidence of generalization. The existing limitation that computational proxies require real-world validation is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 documents the 1 − score transformation and normalization for multi-objective evaluation, adds albuterol and celecoxib prompts for the open-source models, and reports runtimes and API constraints. Hardware, GPT-4 checkpoint information, and code access were already supplied in v1; the new reproducibility statement mainly consolidates existing information.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a focused discussion positioning the simple multi-objective selection rules against MOEA/D, NSGA-III, and recent molecular optimization frameworks. Genetic GFN and Tartarus references also appear. The central positioning of LLMs as molecular genetic operators remains unchanged; alternate publication references for existing works are not new research contributions.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained, with localized corrections and expanded explanations. Future work moves to Appendix A.2, experimental details move into Appendix B, and a reproducibility statement is added. Citation style changes to author–year, but the narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains eleven task rows and a comparator column, and seven new appendix tables present additional comparisons and analyses. Figure 1 adds molecular-string and computational annotations; Figure 2 adds the random-edit curve; Figure A1 adds comparator curves. The Pareto visualization moves from main-text Figure 4 to appendix Figure A3, alongside broader conference-layout changes.

improvement.justification: Expanding from 12 to 23 PMO tasks and adding Augmented Memory and DST materially strengthens the limited comparison coverage in v1. Framework-transfer tests and runtime analyses also address portability and whether oracle savings translate into practical efficiency. These substantially improve the empirical basis, although broad superiority wording remains insufficiently qualified: v3 Table 1 shows Augmented Memory outperforming all MOLLEO variants on ranolazine_mpo.
